and participating in the TCRF at the time of sale and the passenger is located in California at the time of payment. Eligible passengers may

failed to forward to a proper provider or such money was not refunded to you when required. The maximum amount which may be paid by 
the TCRF to any one passenger is the total amount paid on behalf of the passenger to the seller of travel, not to exceed 515.000. A claim 
must be submitted to the TCRF within 12 months after the scheduled completion date of the travel. A claim must include sufficient 
documentation to prove your claim and a $35 processing fee. Claimants must agree to waive their right to other civil remedies against a 
registered participating seller of travel for matters arising out of a sale for which you file a TCRF claim. You may request a claim form by 
writing to: Travel Consumer Restitution Corporation: P.O. Box 6001: Larkspur. CA 94977-6001: or by visiting TCRC's website at:

2007 Business Jet Forecast - We Expect Market to Move Higher 
Project nearly 900 deliveries in 2007 - We believe bizjet deliveries 
can continue to move higher beyond 2006. Our forecast is supported by our 
recent survey results as well as underlying demand drivers including strong 
international growth, increasing replacement demand, and an expanding addressable 
market (fractional/card). Ultimately, we believe deliveries this 
cycle could exceed 1,000. 
International markets growing faster than V.S. - We have found that an 
increasing proportion of bizjets are going to overseas buyers as the 
international market is growing 108 per year. We believe that international 
bizjet demand will continue to grow faster than U.S. driven by expanding 
economies in Eastern Europe/Soviet Union, Middle East oil wealth, early stage 
markets in Asia (China)/India, and a weak dollar. 
Replacement demand could be significant - We believe the replacement of 
older aircraft could serve as a significant driver of bizjet demand as 
the average age of the bizjet fleet is 15 years, older than the commercial 
fleet. The fractional fleet, while relatively young, is now approaching its 
first significant replacement cycle as many aircraft purchased during the 
late 1990s build-up are set to be parted out. 
Reiterate Buy ratings on GD and TXT - We expect GD (Buy 2) and TXT 
(Buy 1) to continue to benefit from business jet upside. 
Please see our full note attached. 
David

Reliable Source 
4/25/02 
This Sunday at noon, C-SPAN ll's "Book TV' will air a sound-only version of Bill Clinton's remarks at a 
party last week in honor of Rep. Peter King's new novel, "Deliver Us From Evil." That's because 
cameraman Richard Hall was prevented from videotaping Clinton at the Dubliner bar. 
Hall told us he started rolling when Clinton showed up unexpectedly. After a few seconds, a King aide 
told Hall that Clinton's people wanted him to stop. Hall continued taping for another 15 seconds, until a 
strapping young man calling himself Doug him to stop. "The president is a private citizen and doesn't 
want cameras on him all the time," Doug barked. Hall assumed he was a Secret Service agent and 
complied. 
After his remarks, Clinton made a beeline for Hall. "Glad you're here!" the former president gushed. "I 
wish you had allowed me to tape your speech' Hall replied. A distressed Clinton asked, "What do you 
mean?" As Hall explained the situation, he heard Doug mutter, "Thanks a lot!" Then an apparently angry 
Clinton gave Doug hell. Nevertheless, Hall said, when he resumed videotaping, Doug came up and shut 
him down again. 
It turns out that Doug Band is Clinton's personal aide, not a Secret Service agent, and had no authority to 
stop C-SPAN's camera. We hear he's now remorseful, but Clinton press secretary Julia Payne declined 
to produce him. "It's well known all over the world," she said, "that Doug has left many a cameraman in 
his wake."

The Band Plays On 
It'/z Last time we checked in with Douglas Band -- former president Bill Clinton's personal aide, who is so 
stern and strapping that he's often mistaken for a Secret Service agent — he was shutting down a C-
SPAN cameraman trying to tape Clinton's remarks at a book party for Rep. Peter King (R-N.Y.). 
Now we hear that when Clinton's young protector isn't blocking pesky reporters from bothering his boss at 
a Washington fundraiser, Band is snuggling with a famous supermodel at a trendy Manhattan restaurant. 
First the fundraiser story: Washington Times metro reporter Jabeen Bhatti was assigned to cover the 
party at the home of Beth and Ron Dozoretz for the Daniel Pearl Foundation. Spotting Clinton, Bhatti told 
us yesterday, she walked toward him through the crowd with notebook ready when Band blocked her 
path. "It's inappropriate to ask any questions' she quoted Band as instructing her at an event held to 
celebrate a free and unfettered press. Bhatti regrouped and tried again. "Why do you think it's important 
to be here?" she innocuously asked Clinton — who turned away in response, she said. 
Now the interesting stuff: Monday's New York Daily News reported that Naomi Campbell was seen 
"snuggling' with a new man at Serafina. We have it on good authority that the man was Band. 
Campbell's publicist, Howard Rubenstein, told us the two are "just friends." Unfortunately Band did not 
respond to a message we left yesterday, and there was no comment, none at all, from the Clinton camp.

help in securing an interview for this amazing 93-year-old rescuer of Czech 
Jewish children. 
Much water has flowed under the traditional bridge since you interviewed me 
on your N channel in 1994 on the launch of my book, 3 years after my 
husband Robert MaxwellICAs death, and more recently when we met for dinner at 
Ghislaineia2s New York apartment. 
You have crowned your career with a spectacular trophy, on which I am 
pleased to congratulate you. Meanwhile, I have carried on with my enduring 
interest in the history of the Holocaust and Jewish Christian relations. 
It was whilst working in this field in 1986, that I discovered the 
extraordinary life of Nicholas Winton, a righteous gentile who saved 669 
Czech children from certain death at the hands of the Nazis by organising 
their transport to England, leaving behind their courageous parents and 
EFTA_R1_01278042 
EFTA02332294
--- PAGE 2 ---
siblings who were later all sent to Auschwitz and murdered. Many of the 
rescued children eventually made their way to the United States. 
A 35mm documentary film in Dolby Digital Sound, made by the Czech Director, 
Matej Minac and entitled Nicholas Winton ICA The Power of Good, will be 
premiered in New York on Wednesday, September 18, 2002 at 7:00 pm, in 
SYMPHONY SPACE, Peter Jay Sharp Theatre, at Broadway and 95th Street, New 
York. It recounts the story of courage and determination of one man, like 
Oscar Schindler and Raoul Wallenberg who cared for Others. Mr. Winton is 
one of the last living rescuers; he is now 93 and has been persuaded to 
travel by Concorde from England for the New York. opening. He will be in New 
York from 14th to 21st September, accompanied by some of the reAchildrenra2 he 
rescued. Whilst in New York, he will be awarded the American Joint 
Distribution Committee Prize (they are also one of the main organizers of 
the event). It is unlikely, in view of his age that he will ever come to 
New York again and I do believe that it would be 
/21CA 
- 2 - 
fitting if his exploits were brought to the knowledge of the American public 
through some of the best American TV shows, such as Larry King Live or the 
Oprah Winfrey show or any suitable program of your choice. 
Nicholas WintotheAs active humanitarian approach to life resulted not only in 
the rescue of 669 children, but also in the construction of a whole chain of 
houses of elderly 'IV/Minton housesIt1% for the elderly in Britain, and many 
projects for handicapped children or the street children in Rio de Janeiro. 
He has much to say to it'Apresentit% day audience, especially after the terrorist 
attacks of September 11th and the endless suicide killings in Israel. He is 
the living example of the courage to care. 
Your presence at the premiere would be a great honour to Nicholas Winton, 
and his many friends in Great Britain and Czechoslovakia, and would of 
course signify the US publicIz:As recognition for his efforts done 60 years 
ago, which could still repeated in our present day situation and remain a 
beacon for future generations. However, having only just been called upon 
myself to help, I do realise that it is very late in the day for such a 
request and would perfectly understand that with your very busy schedule you 
might not be able to attend. But if you could use your considerable 
influence to procure a space for my old and dear friend on one of the main 
TV shows, I would consider it a great personal favour. 
The Czech sponsors are prepared to send by FedEx either to you or any one 
you suggest, the whole package of materials, plus a tape of the film in 
NTSC. 
Thank you in advance for considering my double request and in the hope that 
our paths will cross again in the not too distant future, I send you my very 
best regards and best wishes for your success in your challenging new 
position. 
Yours most sincerely, 
Elisabeth

If I knew it would be the last time 
I'd hear your voice lifted up in praise, 
I would video tape each action and word 
so I could play them back day after day. 
If I knew it would be the last time 
I could spare an extra minute, 
to stop and say "I LOVE YOU" 
instead of assuming you would know I do. 
If I knew it would be the last time 
I would be there to share your day, 
Well I'm sure you'll have so many more, 
so I can let just this one slip away. 
For surely there's always tomorrow 
to make up for an overnight, 
and we always get a second chance 
to make everything just right. 
There will always be another day 
to say "I love you', 
And certainly there's another chance 
to say our "anything I can do?" 
But just in case I might be wrong 
and today is all I get, 
I'd like to say how much I love you 
and I hope we never forget. 
Tomorrow is not promised to anyone, 
young or old alike, 
And today may be the last chance 
you get to hold your loved one tight. 
So if you're waiting for tomorrow, 
why not do it today? 
For if tomorrow never comes, 
you'll surely regret the day. 
That you didn't take extra time 
for a smile, a hug, or a kiss 
and you were too busy to grant someone, 
what turned out to be their one last wish. 
So hold your loved ones close today 
and whisper in their ear, 
Tell them how much you love them 
and that you'll always hold them dear. 
Take time to say "I'm sorry," 
"Please forgive me," "Thank You," or "It's OK" 
And if tomorrow never comes, 
you'll have no regrets about today. 
EFTA_R1_01278051

and last year, i awoke from a deep sleep at 6am in LA, screaming and crying and 
praying, because i felt like the walls were falling in. not on me, but on other 
people. i've never had a panic attack ever, but for a half hour, i was wailing 
and staring at the walls, and couldn't shake the feeling that something really 
horrible was happening, or was about to happen, and that i needed to pray for 
people. my friend called me at 6:30 am to tell me that at 9 am, new york time, 
the planes had hit the world trade center and the pentagon. it all happened at 
the very moment i woke up screaming. kind of weird. who knows... 
anyway, 
last night, i had a dream i was flying a helicopter. all night i kept dreaming 
of flying a helicopter, and i wasn't very good at it. i was all over the place. 
and then i was on the ground, watching myself fly it around. and it crashed in 
the backyard of some poor, ethnic-type people's house. 
and today, i read about 
the crash in afghanistan that killed seven people. not that weird, but just 
another in a string of dreams that ended up bearing some resemblance to the news 
later in the day. 
and... in the dream, you were in the cockpit with me at some point. very 
briefly. you weren't in it when it went down. 
(sometimes i have visions of happy things, too.) 
ho ho ho. 
Jeff

Ms. Maxwell, 
I left you and Jeffrey some unusual fruit on your kitchen counter. I labeled each fruit with your chef. They are 
not ripe now, however, in about 2-3 days they should soften up and be ready for eating. Two of the fruit are 
football-shaped with a tan, coarse outside. They are called Mameys. We are growing them in the kitchen 
garden. You can eat them when they soften. You can cut them in half and eat them plain with a spoon, like a 
melon, or mix a little cool whip or whip cream with the meat. It is native to Cuba and "shakes" are a very popular 
way to consume them there or in Miami. The second one is smaller and with smooth tan outside. It is a 
Sapodilla. Wait till it softens and then eat with a spoon. It is tangy or almost spicy. The third one is round and 
green. It is called a chocolate pudding fruit because the meat inside looks just like chocolate pudding. I like to 
mix it with some whip cream to cut the sweetness of the chocolate flavor. Some use the fresh fruit as a 
substitute to bananas when making banana bread. It is great that way too. At any rate, I hope you get the 
chance to try them all. 
There are 2 21- and 3 1r terra cotta containers unused on the property. I suggest we can use these,

flowering Crown of Thoms (there is a tall specimen near the MBR doors, facing west- (white, pink or red), 
unusual Aloes (big), Agaves(big), palms, or Bromeliads ( some flower spikes last about 3-5 months. depending 
on what specie). I would like to use some unusual specimens as well as hardy plants like Aloes, Bromeliads, 
Crowns, Agaves or Palms in these containers. Soft growing flowering plants really don't do well as a container 
garden. IF you need photos, I can email you some soon of those species that might interest you. I don't know 
if I ever informed you of my web site- 
It displays some good photos of the Aloes, Agaves 
in the product- succulent areas. Bromeliads are listed too. Please let me know what you like and I will price it 
out for you.
